item.title: The Political Earthquake From Germany’s China Shock

Competition from China shakes that bargain to its foundations.

item.title: Does Claude Have Rights?

item.title: A Congress for Europe’s Future
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's recently proposed Congress of Europe is a step in the right direction, given the scale of Europe's geopolitical challenges. But to succeed, it must address the shortcomings that have hampered similar efforts in the past.

item.title: Can Adaptation Accelerate Climate Action?
item.description: After a summer of apocalyptic headlines, a new survey finds that people across the political spectrum are deeply concerned about preparing for the effects of global warming. The adaptation imperative may end up being the kind of crisis that forces us to stop neglecting the green agenda and act at the necessary scale.

item.title: Trump’s Iran Sanctions Have a China Problem
item.description: US President Donald Trump is trying to pressure the Iranian regime by isolating it from the dollar-based financial system. But because Iran’s oil trade largely moves through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks, those sanctions increasingly depend on financial institutions beyond American control.
